newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-Australia may seek to drop New Delhi venue.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Australia may seek to drop New Delhi venue.

text.p: Australia are considering asking Indian cricket officials to drop New Delhi as a venue on future tours after complaining about the city's high pollution levels, The Australian newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Several Australian players have suffered eye and respiratory problems while staying in the city during their current five-week tour of India, the newspaper said.

"The pollution in Delhi is such that we should give serious consideration before coming back to play any more cricket here," team manager and Australian Cricket Board (ACB) director Cam Battersby told the newspaper from India.
Australia are due to return to India for a three-test match tour in 1998, but The Australian said ACB officials will oppose Delhi as a match venue.
ACB officials in Australia were not available for comment.
The paper said tour management believe it is unfair and hazardous to subject professional players to such conditions.
"I've heard it said that Delhi is the fourth most polluted city in the world -- if that's so, I'd like to see the other three," Battersby said.
"It really starts getting to you after a while."
By the time Australia leave India in early November, they will have spent almost half the tour in New Delhi.
Mark Taylor's side lost a one-off test match against India two weeks ago and are languishing in third place in a triangular limited overs tournament involving their hosts and South Africa.
"I think most people at home would be quite horrified at the amount of pollution the guys played in (in New Delhi)," team physiotherapist Errol Alcott told The Australian.
"The pollution is really bad -- it's terrible. It's an irritant to the eyes, the nose, the upper respiratory tract, the back of the throat," Alcott said.
"I don't think any one performance has been affected by the pollution problems but over a period of time it does wear on you. It's just another facet."
